collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DEPARTURES AND EXILE (DEP-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Leaving and being left: moving huts, short journeys, visitors going home, goodbyes done well and badly, homesickness, and the rare person who sails away for good. Choosing to leave is never a rejection of one's people, and choosing to stay is never a failure.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult)

collection.description: A villager finally sets off to live by the far lagoon, then sits down on the hilltop: unpack, or keep the bag packed by the door.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: For years (name1) has said that one day (he/she) will go and live by the big lagoon on the other side of the island, where the water is calm and the fishing is easy. This morning (he/she) finally packed everything, said goodbye, and walked out of the village. (He/she) got as far as the top of the hill, sat down, and has been sitting there for some time.

choices.label: Leave the Bag Packed by the Door

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (name1) walks back down the hill and puts everything back where it was. A few people look surprised. Most just say hello. (name1) feels foolish for about an hour, and then, unexpectedly, relieved. (He/she) wanted the dream of the lagoon more than the lagoon. That turns out to be allowed.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (name1) comes back but doesn't unpack. The bag sits by the door, ready. Some days (he/she) looks at it and thinks, tomorrow. Some days (he/she) forgets it's there. It's comforting to have it. (He/she) doesn't know yet whether (he/she) will ever pick it up, and for now that's fine.
